- MT: Multi-Teaming: Two timekeepers at same level with same area of expertise should not handle identical task within same time frame. Only one timekeeper. So no.

If the timekeeper's core focus is not litigation? We don't know. But likely research for motion to compel is within litigation. So maybe not.

- PT: Paralegal Task: Attorney level personnel should spend minimal time on tasks typically delegated to paralegals (docketing, preparation of entity formation documents, document review, bate stamping). Research for motion to compel is not paralegal. So no.

- PTI: Personnel Transition Inefficiencies: Time associated with a transitioning timekeeper becoming familiar with a new matter. Not indicated.

- PYR: Pyramiding: Legal professional rate should not be charged for task(s) not requiring legal training, knowledge or judgment (e.g., reviewing newspaper articles re: lawsuit). Research for motion to compel likely requires legal knowledge. So no.
